rounds.text: Rajshree Polypack Ltd is deeply undervalued relative to its intrinsic worth, trading at a steep discount with a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 70 per share against its current market price of Rs 21.1 [E44]. This offers an enormous margin of safety of 69.7% [E45], while a reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in an overly pessimistic -2.6% earnings growth against a base case of 14.0% [E46]. Valuation metrics reinforce this disconnect, with the stock trading at a modest P/E of 9.09x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.83x [E2], representing a dramatic discount to sector benchmarks such as a 25.58x sector P/E and a 2.22x sector P/B [E6, E7]. Fundamental momentum supports the bullish case, highlighted by a robust 20% growth in compounded profit over the trailing twelve months [E21], a quarterly operating margin expansion of 4 percentage points year-over-year to 16% [E30], and solid cash backing where operating cash flow reached Rs 19 Cr in March 2026 [E34]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen awards the company a strong 90 out of 100 score [E63], underpinned by a high relative-strength rating of 98 against the Nifty 500 [E50] and technical strength with the price sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49]. conceded: [E4, E22, E38, E40, E42, E59, E60, E61, E62]

Rajshree Polypack Ltd (RPPL) carries significant structural risks and insider desertion that undermine its headline-driven valuation appeal. Promoters have aggressively slashed their stake to 44.22% as of June 2026, down 8.26 percentage points from September 2023 [E40], alongside a parallel retreat by domestic institutions from 4.28% to 1.08% [E42]. Compounded share price growth has cratered across every major time horizon, resulting in a -16% return over 1 year, -7% over 3 years, and -4% over 5 years [E22, E23, E24], culminating in a severe twelve-month price drop of -20.1% [E51]. Fundamental wealth creation remains sluggish, with a low median return on equity of 9% over both the 3-year and 5-year periods [E26, E27] and an outright lack of dividend payouts despite repeated profits [E59]. Furthermore, the business is burdened by mounting debt of Rs 123 Cr in Mar 2026 [E38] and massive contingent liabilities totaling Rs 122 Cr [E61]. Conceded: the company trades at an attractive price-to-book of 0.83x [E2] with a low P/E of 9.09x [E1], while generating positive annual free cash flow of Rs 7 Cr [E35] alongside a robust 12-month profit growth of 20% [E21]. However, extreme annualised volatility of 53.5% [E53] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.9% [E52] highlight that these discounted multiples reflect deep, persistent underlying risks rather than a mispriced bargain.

Conceded: promoters hold 44.22% as of June 2026 down from 52.48% in September 2023 [E40], and domestic institutions hold 1.08% down from 4.28% [E42]. However, institutional money flow reads POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with a holding change of +1.08 percentage points [E43], counterbalancing the institutional narrative. Conceded: historical share price growth has been negative over 1, 3, and 5 years [E22, E23, E24], but this divergence is explicitly classified as fundamentals-led where profit grew 14% against a price decline of -4% over 5 years, signaling an underappreciated asset [E55]. Conceded: the business carries borrowings of Rs 123 Cr [E38] and contingent liabilities of Rs 122 Cr [E61], yet it produces real financial output with operating cash flow of Rs 19 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 7 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, profits are fully backed by cash with a cash conversion of 1.12x [E33]. Finally, while volatility and drawdowns are high [E52, E53], the stock price is above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with the 50-day above the 200-day [E49], showing immediate technical strength that aligns with a rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 [E63].

Conceded: institutional money flow reads positive money flow with a holding change of +1.08 percentage points [E43]. However, this minor fluctuation does nothing to mask the broad institutional and insider flight, evidenced by domestic institutions collapsing from 4.28% to 1.08% and promoters slashing their stake from 52.48% to 44.22% [E40, E42]. Conceded: the 5-year profit growth outpaces the -4% share price decline [E22, E55], but labeling this a divergence hides the persistent wealth destruction of a 16% one-year price drop and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.9% [E24, E52]. Conceded: the business generated Rs 19 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 7 Cr in free cash flow with a 1.12x cash conversion [E33, E34, E35]. Yet that cash generation is heavily overshadowed by massive financial overhangs, including Rs 123 Cr in borrowings and a staggering Rs 122 Cr in contingent liabilities [E38, E61]. Finally, pointing to technical moving averages and a high screen score [E49, E63] ignores the severe underlying reality of high annualised volatility at 53.5%, a weak Sharpe ratio of 0.29, and a miserable 3-year return on equity stuck at a low 9% [E27, E53, E54, E60].
